Information about inquiry drafts, browser storage and the product details on this site.
Your inquiry

The form creates an email draft in your browser. It does not send your information to LZZ or upload drawings. To contact us, open the draft in your email app, add your attachments and send it yourself.
Saved drafts

The form saves your input and draft status in the current tab using sessionStorage, with a separate entry for each selected part. Your details stay available after a refresh but are not saved to an account or sent to LZZ. Select "Clear saved input" to remove the entry for the current part.

Your browser may restore this data when it restores a previous session. Clear your input before leaving a shared device. If browser storage is blocked or full, you can still use the form while the page is open. Select "Save draft" to download a text copy.
Cookies and external services
This site does not use analytics or advertising cookies. Your email provider, WhatsApp and other linked websites have their own privacy policies.
Product and company information

Product pages use catalog photographs and clearly labeled illustrative visuals. Neither is an inspection record or a specification document. Original workshop photographs and company documents are identified separately from product examples.

Product pages use shorter titles and summaries of the catalog entries. Original catalog names and source material are retained in our archive; they are not displayed on every product page. The summaries are not independently verified specifications for the photographed parts. Confirm material grades and tolerances with the team, along with the inspection and commercial terms for your order.

The engineering guides help you prepare an inquiry; they are not inspection records or customer case studies. They do not establish suitability for a particular application. blocks.text: CNC milling vs turning vs 5-axis machining: how to choose
On this page

A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence.
CNC turning operation; original LZZ process photograph.
CNC milling operation photographed in LZZ process materials; source folder dated December 2025.
Five-axis machining operation; original LZZ process photograph.
Compare the processes by geometry
CNC turning
Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis.
Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling.
CNC milling
Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces.
Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records.
Multi-axis machining
Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches.
Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model.
When does a part need more than one process?

A shaft with cross-holes, a turned fitting with milled flats or a housing with angled faces may need more than one operation or setup. The route should preserve the relationships between critical features. Send a 3D model and controlled 2D drawing so the team can review datums, access and inspection together.
Is 5-axis machining always more accurate?

No single process label guarantees accuracy. Acceptance depends on the part geometry, machine and setup, datum strategy, material, finishing and measurement method. If an interface matters, state its tolerance and datum on the drawing and ask how it will be produced and checked. Any tolerance target needs feature-specific review.
What should I include when asking for a process recommendation?
A 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing revision.

Identify the working surfaces

For a housing or shaft, the surfaces that meet other parts matter as much as the outside shape. The same applies to a mounting block. Mark the surfaces that locate, seal, slide or carry load on the drawing so you can discuss tolerances in relation to their function.
Compare milled pockets and housings with turned shafts and fittings. Some designs need both operations; the geometry determines the process choice.
Specify critical dimensions

Give the datums and mating details for critical features, with their acceptance limits. A 3D model shows the shape but may leave fits or surface texture undefined. It may also omit edge conditions and measurement methods. Include a controlled 2D drawing when these requirements apply.

Tolerances need review against the specific drawing. The material and feature geometry affect the assessment, as do the setup and measurement method; a single tolerance cannot apply to every catalog part. Agree on inspection requirements and supporting records for your design.
Specify material and finish

State the exact alloy or plastic grade and any material-certificate requirement. For coated parts, specify the finish and whether critical dimensions apply before or after treatment. Mark areas that need masking, cosmetic faces and burr-sensitive edges.
The material and finish checklist covers these details. Catalog photographs show shapes and surfaces; they cannot establish a coating specification or provide material certification.
Agree on prototype checks

Explain the purpose of the prototype. You may need to check assembly fit and access, assess appearance or run a functional test. Agree on the checks needed for revision or approval. If the design changes, issue a revised drawing with the affected dimensions identified; an email description alone is not enough.

Quotes & ordering
What is the minimum order quantity?
Orders start at 1 piece. Include your first-order quantity and expected repeat quantities so the quotation can distinguish prototype work from future batches.
What is the production lead time?

Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. Record the confirmed production schedule and delivery arrangements in your quotation and order.
Preparing a quotation
What should I send for a quotation?
Please provide the following information:
Drawing revision and units
Exact material grade and condition
Finish and surface treatment
First-order and expected repeat quantities
Delivery destination

Dimensioned 2D drawing with critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirements
Does the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing?

No. The inquiry form prepares an email draft. Check the draft, open it in your email application, attach your drawings and send it there. Copy and download options are also available; preparing a draft does not send an inquiry to LZZ.
Processes & specifications
Which machining services can I discuss with LZZ?

Our five service areas are CNC milling, CNC turning, five-axis CNC machining, plastic machining and casting machining. Share the complete part geometry so the route, workholding and finishing requirements can be reviewed together. For castings, agree who supplies and approves the blank.
How should I specify the material and finish?

Specify the exact material grade and condition, not just aluminum, steel or plastic. Identify cosmetic faces, surface treatment requirements, masking and dimensions that must be checked after finishing. The quotation should record the agreed specification.
Can every feature hold ±0.01 mm?

No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional engineering reference for selected critical features after review, not a general part tolerance or guarantee. Material, geometry, setup and measurement method determine whether it applies. Identify each critical feature on the drawing for confirmation.

Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time.

Finishing services and acceptance points

We support deburring, bead blasting, polishing, anodizing, passivation and plating as appropriate to the selected material. The quotation defines the finish and any accompanying documents; not every treatment is suitable for every alloy.
Deburring and polishing: specify edge breaks, cosmetic faces and any controlled roughness.

Specify the material grade

The catalog groups parts by material: aluminum, stainless steel, copper and brass, and engineering plastics. Each group covers different grades. State the grade and condition your design requires, then confirm whether alternatives are permitted and which material documents you need.

How should I compare material options?

Compare named grades against the part's load, weight, temperature, environment, electrical or thermal function and mating components. “Aluminum,” “stainless” or “plastic” alone is not a purchase specification: grade, condition and applicable standard matter. Specify visual appearance separately from the finish's function. Name the required finish standard and revision where applicable, and describe color, gloss, texture, coating thickness or roughness only where these are controlled requirements. Mark masked areas, cosmetic faces and surfaces for corrosion protection, electrical contact or sealing. Tell the supplier whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after finishing. Highlight mating bores, threads and other interfaces where a coating matters. Specify edge breaks and cosmetic faces separately so functional and appearance criteria can be reviewed together.
